--- title: "Initial letter identification" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LECTURA_RF_ESCRIBIR_LETRA_INICIAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LECTURA_RF_ESCRIBIR_LETRA_INICIAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Identificar la letra inicial*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LECTURA_RF_ESCRIBIR_LETRA_INICIAL.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Initial letter identification, from age 5 to 7 (3,793 administrations in 5 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .57. AUC .79–.80 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1884 4047 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 20 (1884) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child selects from 4 options the beginning letter of the name of the object presented on the screen. | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_imagenes.png){width=45%} ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring |Age.term (label 3) | |----:|:----------------------|:----------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|:------------------| | 1884|Escribir Letra Inicial |Un dibujo por pantalla | 20| 4|— |— |fijo |Aciertos |— | **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1884.** 4 de práctica + 20 de prueba; las instrucciones hablan de 5 opciones, pero la pantalla muestra 4. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* ## Theoretical framework Letter knowledge is the ability to recognize each grapheme and associate it with its name or sound. It is the gateway to the **alphabetic principle**. The platform measures it in two ways: naming letters, and choosing the letter with which the name of a picture begins, which also requires isolating the first sound. **What the evidence says.** Together with phonological awareness and rapid naming, it is one of the three major predictors of reading. Its weight is similar in English, Spanish and Czech [@caravolas2013growth]. In Spanish, letter knowledge is the best predictor of simple syllable reading; phonological awareness weighs more for complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. The full review of the evidence is in the [letter knowledge pilot task sheet](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/LET.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** Both tasks have very high internal consistency (α = .90 and .97). Letter naming is stable between terms (ρ = .73) and predicts low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency years later with a median AUC of .71. As a skill with a ceiling, it discriminates mainly at ages 4 and 5. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.3| 2011| 159|2016/17 | 881| 0| 881| 34| | 5.3| 2013| 630|2018/19 | 679| 417| 262| 33| | 6.1| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 918| 264| 653| 34| | 6.1| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 780| 0| 780| 31| | 6.2| 2015| 950|2021/22 | 269| 0| 24| 8| | 7.1| 2014| 950|2021/22 | 266| 0| 0| 8| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 5.3| 417| 2013| 21.32| 4.40| 24| -2.03| 0| 51.80| | 6.1| 264| 2010| 21.83| 3.86| 24| -2.40| 0| 52.65| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–24 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 5.3| 417|6.2–24 |2–24 |0–24 | | | 6.1| 264|6.6–24 |4–24 |0–24 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .57 (median .57, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .90. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2011| 5.3| 6.1| 697| 0.63| 0.57| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (5.3, r = .55); Phonological awareness (6.1, r = .66); Phonological awareness (6.2, r = .13); Phonological awareness (7.1, r = .22). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .79–.80. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.69. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LECTURA_RF_ESCRIBIR_LETRA_INICIAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .65–.73 (2 time points; 435–512 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.3| 417| 2013| 11.0| 15.0| 18| 21| 24| 24| 24| | 6.1| 264| 2010| 12.2| 17.0| 20| 22| 24| 24| 24| | 6.2| 269| 2015| 0.0| 9.6| 20| 22| 23| 24| 24| | 7.1| 266| 2014| 0.0| 21.0| 22| 23| 24| 24| 24| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LECTURA_RF_ESCRIBIR_LETRA_INICIAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 1,560| 0.132| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 1,554| 0.118| 0.019| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 1,552| 0.146| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 1,560| 0.145| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 1,685| 0.162| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 1,693| 0.131| 0.006| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 1,688| 0.105| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 1,698| 0.100| | |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 225| 0.082| 0.540| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 267| 0.063| 0.305| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 269| 0.053| | |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 263| 0.162| 0.187| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 263| 0.055| 0.374| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 266| 0.019| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Initial letter identification” (codes 1884 and 4047; LEEDUCA battery) assesses alphabetic knowledge (phoneme–grapheme mapping). Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 24 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 6 sessions, from 5 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .90 (N = 3,273, 24 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .57. Stability across time points was ρ = .57. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.69. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.3, 6.1 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - The task has several codes (versions or forms): check that time points are comparable before pooling norms. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
